seed: A guide names the tool it is teaching. The tool bar does not always have that tool's own button on it: three shapes share one slot and it wears whichever one you reached for last, and a narrow window pushes the last slots into a More menu. This walk drives Frames are screens in a NARROW window, where both are true at once. Every step must still point at a real control and the card must carry one line saying which button the tool is inside, instead of falling to the middle of the window with no ring at all. Neither step may open anything: the person opens the menu themselves and the guide only moves on when they really take the tool. The toolbar-*.json files beside the shots say which slots were on the bar at the time, so what each step fell back to is recorded rather than assumed.

steps.note: the guide brought its own window and this walk gave it a narrow one, so the bar has gone compact: the last slots are behind the More button at its end, and the shapes slot is wearing the line because nobody has drawn a shape yet

THE FIRST TEST: the frame tool has no button of its own on this bar. The ring must be on the More button at the end of it, and the card must carry the line saying the frame tool is in that menu and to open it. Before this the card fell to the middle of the window with no ring.
the step still waited for the person: nothing opened the menu for them, and nothing moved on until F really landed
what is on the bar at the moment the guide asks for the rectangle

THE SECOND TEST: the rectangle has no button of its own either, because the shapes slot is still wearing the line. The ring must be on the button holding it, which is the shapes slot while that slot is on the bar and the More button once it is not, and the card must say which and how to reach the rectangle.
THE THIRD TEST: the extra line only shows while the tool is hidden. Taking the rectangle made the slot wear it, so a step naming the rectangle from here rings its own button and says nothing extra.
the guide closed and left the window alone
